news.content:
Meta Platforms Inc. (NASDAQ:META) will give shareholders a new class of non-voting stock in January, letting CEO Mark Zuckerberg keep control while the company gains a new way to raise money to fund its artificial intelligence buildout.

How Meta’s Class C Shares Work

Meta’s board declared a dividend of one share of Class C common stock for each outstanding share of Class A and Class B common stock, as part of a “recapitalization” that takes effect Jan. 19, 2027

The Class C shares carry no voting rights, Meta said in a filing with the U.S. Securities and Exchange Commission.

Shareholders won’t vote on the change, since entities tied to Zuckerberg and his wife, Priscilla Chan, that hold 56.1% of Meta’s voting power approved it on Tuesday.

Meta said the shares let it raise capital, pay employees and fund acquisitions without diluting voting power, and that it expects to sell Class C stock from time to time.

Read Also: 'Live by the Sword, Die by the Sword': Elon Musk Warns Those Who 'Pick Fights' as Democrats Reportedly Weigh Probing Him After Midterms

Market Watchers Weigh in

Helene Meisler, technical analyst at TheStreet, said on X that she applauds the split but that 2-for-1 is “paltry for a $700 stock.”

She added that an 8-for-1 ratio would have been better.

Nicholas Mugalli, CEO and principal of World Trade Securities, saw the plan for “a non-voting currency to fund AI, acquisitions and engineer pay” as a sign of “more capex coming,” with 2026 capex already guided at $135 billion to $145 billion.

An equity investor Sandeep Anand said that “shareholders absorb 100% of the economic dilution of future issuance; Zuckerberg absorbs none of the control dilution.”

Alphabet Inc. took a similar route in 2014, splitting its stock 2-for-1 to create non-voting shares. Nvidia Corp., Apple Inc. and Amazon.com, Inc. have also split in recent years.

Meta Beats Estimates on Revenue and Earnings

For the third quarter, Meta posted revenue of $64.6 billion, beating analyst estimates of $63.37 billion, according to Benzinga Pro. Adjusted earnings were $7.40 per share, beating estimates of $5.74.

Meta expects fourth-quarter revenue of $73 billion to $76 billion versus estimates of $73.74 billion.

Price Action: On Wednesday, shares closed 0.47% higher at $697.52 and rose 2.17% to $712.65 in extended trading on the results announcement that came in after the bell.

news.content:
Meta Platforms, Inc. (NASDAQ:META) CEO Mark Zuckerberg sees a potentially lucrative future for its Muse AI assistant, but Deepwater Asset Management’s Gene Munster warns that the product is already burning cash at an alarming rate.

Muse AI Gains Traction With Shoppers

During the company’s third-quarter earnings call, Zuckerberg said Meta’s family of apps now reaches 3.64 billion daily users, while Threads has surpassed Elon Musk’s X in monthly active users.

He highlighted Muse’s early momentum, saying more than 10 million people in the U.S. and Canada had set up personal AI agents in about six weeks. Roughly 25% of those users engage with Muse on any given day.

Shopping has emerged as the assistant’s most popular use case, with purchases averaging more than $200, Zuckerberg said. Users are also connecting Muse to email, calendars and other services to improve productivity.

"Now that Muse has clear product-market fit, we are entering a new phase and a more operational phase that is focused on scaling," Zuckerberg said.

Read Also: Mark Zuckerberg Keeps Control as Meta Adds Class C Stock — Analyst Sees ‘More Capex Coming’ for AI

Gene Munster Warns of Muse AI’s Costly Growth

Munster offered a more cautious assessment on X.

"Even though there are only around 10m daily Muse users (my estimate), the product is losing a lot of money, more than any other products they’ve launched," Munster wrote.

He said Zuckerberg believes the economics will eventually work as Meta expands computing capacity and earns fees from commerce transactions.

Futurum Equities’ chief market strategist Shay Boloor also took to X and said, "Zuckerberg says Muse could eventually generate more revenue per user than Facebook and Instagram with shopping already its most popular use and purchases averaging ~$200."

He added that the AI assistant could help Meta build a new commerce business alongside its established advertising platform.

During the call, Zuckerberg outlined additional monetization plans, including subscriptions for advanced AI capabilities, paid business services and transaction fees from purchases facilitated by Muse.

Meta expects to improve Muse’s computing efficiency more than tenfold over the next year, Zuckerberg said, helping the product move toward profitability as revenue scales.

Meta Raises Spending Outlook Despite Earnings Beat

Meta reported third-quarter revenue of $64.6 billion, beating analyst estimates of $63.37 billion. Adjusted earnings of $7.40 per share also topped expectations of $5.74.

Meta now expects full-year 2026 expenses to total $175 billion to $179 billion, up from its earlier forecast of $165 billion to $169 billion, after a $9.9 billion charge related to third-quarter legal proceedings.

Price Action: Meta shares rose 2.17% in after-hours trading to $712.65, following a regular-session close at $697.52, according to Benzinga Pro.

Following Tesla Inc.‘s (NASDAQ:TSLA) Q3 earnings call on Wednesday, investors Gene Munster of Deepwater Asset Management and Dan Ives think that the company’s Full Self-Driving (FSD) technology remains a critical piece of the company’s business strategy.

TSLA Stock Falls as Investors Digest Lower CapEx Outlook

In a post on the social media platform X, Munster shared his ‘Pressure Points’ video where he described that Tesla stock was declining because Tesla had its “capex a little bit lower in the December quarter” and that because investors were focused on the “long-term opportunity, you want more capex.”

Read Also: Tesla Cybercabs Could Reach Customers by End of 2026, but Elon Musk Says Vast Majority Will Be TSLA-Owned

The investor then shifted focus to the FSD service, which he said was at an “inflection point” following Tesla’s latest figures from its earnings report. He said that Tesla added about 250,000 FSD subscriptions in Q3 and that the number of FSD miles driven was up 190% YoY.

Munster said that Tesla offering customers the opportunity to add their cars to the Robotaxi fleet sometime in 2027 Q2 was a “big step forward” for the company.

Gene Munster Hails Ashok Elluswamy

The investor pointed to Tesla AI Lead Ashok Elluswamy‘s response when an analyst asked if the company would be affected by traditional automakers partnering with companies like Nvidia Corp. (NASDAQ:NVDA) to develop Level 2+ self-driving systems.

“It’s easy to get to the first 90% and make a cool-looking demo,” Elluswamy said, but added that the final ten percent was “difficult” and “long-tailed” to get to self-driving without any injuries or accidents. “People don’t realize anyone with their sane mind should not attempt to solve this problem,” he said.

Elluswamy then said that as Tesla releases unsupervised FSD to its customer fleet, he did not think that Tesla’s rivals could “match it in several years.” Munster hailed Elluswamy’s response, saying that the FSD service would “blow you away,” urging people to try it.

Read Also: Gary Black Predicts SPCX to Offer $420 Per Share For TSLA in a Stock-For-Stock Deal, Calls Tesla-SpaceX Merger ‘Inevitable’

Munster also pointed to Musk’s comments during the earnings call, where he said that customers coming into Tesla showrooms were asking for FSD demos and not a particular product like the Cybertruck or the Model Y.

The investor said that considering the FSD system’s progress, its “incremental value” to drive sales, as well as the potential around Robotaxis, the “momentum” around Tesla was picking up.

“So, big picture, FSD is working. It’s working for Tesla. It’s going to be really hard for traditional automotive to close that gap,” the investor said in the video.

Dan Ives Doubles Down on Tesla-SpaceX Merger

In a post on X, Ives also shared his views following the earnings call. “Tesla FSD continues to drive sales, with attach rates topping 75% of North American deliveries,” Ives said, while also adding that Tesla’s active FSD subscriptions reached 1.74 million, which was up 67% YoY.

“Optimus production has begun as the AI era now takes shape at Tesla which dovetails into SpaceX merger strategic fit,” he added in the post, backing a merger between Tesla and Space Exploration Technologies Corp. (NASDAQ:SPCX) yet again.

Musk, during Tesla’s earnings call, said that producing 20,000 units a week of the Robot at the company’s Fremont, California, facility could take a year or maybe longer. Musk earlier this month said Optimus and Robotaxi could eventually account for the majority of Tesla’s value.

Meta Platforms Inc. (NASDAQ:META) CEO Mark Zuckerberg believes the company can reach superintelligence by scaling up its models, with larger ones already in training that he expects to be far more capable.

‘Methodically’ Climbing the Ladder

Zuckerberg told analysts on the company’s third-quarter earnings call on Wednesday that his view is Meta will be able to “build superintelligence through scaling,” and that the company is “methodically working our way up the ladder.”

Meta is already working on larger models after Muse Wonder, its frontier model, and he expects them to be “very impressive and capable.”

The company plans to keep pushing the frontier models while distilling its models into much smaller, more efficient versions built for personal agents like Muse, which more than 10 million users in the U.S. and Canada have set up.

Read Also: Stock Market: Will S&P 500 Open Up or Down Today?

Cheaper Models, Higher Expectations

Zuckerberg expects Meta to deliver today’s intelligence “at a fraction of the cost” in a smaller model within a year, but does not think “most people are going to want to use the current model level of intelligence” by then.

Revenue, efficiency and model development all have to advance to “fund and support the compute buildout,” he added.

Meta expects 2026 capital expenditures of $135 billion to $145 billion, and CFO Susan Li said the company will “continue investing aggressively” to support its core business and emerging AI initiatives.

Meta also announced it will give shareholders a new class of non-voting shares in January, letting Zuckerberg keep control while the company gains a new way to raise money to fund its AI buildout.

Tops Q3 Estimates, Lifts Expense Outlook

Meta reported third-quarter revenue of $64.6 billion, above analyst estimates of $63.37 billion, according to Benzinga Pro. Adjusted earnings of $7.40 per share also topped the $5.74 expected.

The company now expects full-year 2026 expenses of $175 billion to $179 billion, up from its earlier forecast of $165 billion to $169 billion, including a $9.9 billion charge tied to legal proceedings in the quarter.

Price Action: Meta shares closed 0.47% higher at $697.52 on Wednesday, then rose 2.17% to $712.65 in extended trading after the results.

Former Google CEO Eric Schmidt reportedly holds about 1% of Anthropic PBC through an early investment, potentially giving him one of the largest individual windfalls from the artificial intelligence company’s upcoming public market debut.

Early Series A Bet

Schmidt invested “tens of millions of dollars” in Anthropic’s Series A round, according to a Bloomberg report published Monday, citing people familiar with the matter.

However, it is unclear whether he has sold any stake of his early investment.

A spokesperson for Hiltzik Strategies, the firm representing Schmidt, declined to comment, and Anthropic did not immediately respond to Benzinga’s request.

Schmidt led Google as CEO from 2001 to 2011, overseeing its 2004 public listing, then served as executive chairman.

He kept the role at Alphabet Inc. (NASDAQ:GOOG) (NASDAQ:GOOGL) when it was formed in 2015, before moving into a technology advisory role in 2017.

Read Also: ‘Obviously This Is a Finger’: Apple’s ‘Pro and Tell’ Teaser Has Everyone Talking — MacBook Pro Buzz Intensifies

How Much Schmidt Stands to Gain

Anthropic was valued at $461 million when Schmidt made his investment in 2021, according to data company PitchBook.

Last week, investors indicated the company’s fair valuation was around $1.8 trillion to $2 trillion, Bloomberg said. At the high end of the range, the Claude maker could be valued at more than 4,300 times its Series A funding.

At a $2 trillion valuation, the stake would lift Schmidt’s net worth by about one-third to nearly $80 billion, according to Bloomberg’s wealth index.

With Anthropic’s May valuation of $965 billion, Schmidt could add $10 billion to his current net worth of $57.5 billion, the report added.

Other Backers

Alphabet owns about 14% of Anthropic, a stake that would be worth over $280 billion at a $2 trillion valuation, while Amazon.com, Inc. has invested an estimated $8 billion.

Nvidia Corp. and Microsoft Corp. also made later investments in the Claude maker.

IPO Could Come in Weeks

Anthropic has not formally announced an IPO date. Altimeter Capital’s Brad Gerstner, an early investor, told CNBC last week that he expects the company to go public in “weeks, not months.”

Anthropic told investors that third-quarter revenue rose 45% from the previous quarter to $16.8 billion and that it was profitable on an adjusted basis, Reuters reported.

Editor’s note: This story has been updated with a response from TSMC and SK Hynix.

Samsung Electronics Co. Ltd. (OTC:SSNLF) will reportedly use Taiwan Semiconductor Manufacturing Co. Ltd.’s (NYSE:TSM) process to make the base die for Nvidia Corp.’s (NASDAQ:NVDA) custom high-bandwidth memory.

Nvidia Pushes Suppliers Toward TSMC

In August, Nvidia unveiled NVHBM, a custom design that integrates the memory controller into the base die and can deliver up to 30% more memory bandwidth and 15% lower power consumption than standard HBM4E.

The AI bellwether has asked Samsung, SK Hynix Inc. (NASDAQ:SKHY), and Micron Technology Inc. (NASDAQ:MU), the three suppliers tapped to produce NVHBM, to manufacture the base die, the logic layer at the bottom of the HBM stack, on TSMC’s 3-nanometer process, industry sources told the Seoul Economic Daily.

It also wants the core die to be standardized on the 6th-generation 1c DRAM process.

Samsung’s Device Solutions division accepted the request after an internal review, the report added.

TSMC and SK Hynix declined to comment on the report, saying they do not comment on individual customers. Samsung and Nvidia did not immediately respond to Benzinga’s request for comment.

TSMC declined to comment on the report, saying it does not comment on individual customers.

In a 2024 statement on memory collaboration, the company said it has worked with partners including Micron, Samsung Memory, and SK Hynix on high-bandwidth memory solutions aiming to “tackle the rapidly growing demand in AI.”

Read Also: Stock Market: Will S&P 500 Open Up or Down Today?

TSMC Could Benefit Regardless

Samsung worked with TSMC four years ago on packaging compatibility, but this is the first time the two have partnered at the HBM manufacturing stage, the report said.

Samsung will maintain its turnkey model for standard HBM and custom HBM supplied to other customers.

Chief Market Strategist at Futurum Equities Shay Boloor sees the setup giving Nvidia “more flexibility to shift orders between suppliers as HBM prices rise,” while TSMC stands to benefit “regardless of which memory maker wins the business.”

Shortages and China Cloud the Outlook

JPMorgan’s analysis shows HBM shortages of 20% in 2026, 19% in 2027, and 16% in 2028, with the cumulative shortage reaching 23 weeks by 2028.

Memory chip makers are also facing intensified competition with China, as memory maker ChangXin Memory Technologies reported progress on a denser DRAM design and plans server-memory products using it by the end of 2026.

Meta Platforms Inc. (NASDAQ:META) has struck an agreement designed to keep CEO Mark Zuckerberg in California, addressing the possibility that a proposed billionaire wealth tax could prompt him to relocate.

Zuckerberg agreed to remain a California resident, or live wherever Meta maintains its headquarters, for eight years, the company said on Wednesday. In exchange, he would receive non-voting Class C shares that he could sell if voters approve the proposed billionaire tax, or Proposition 40, next month. The proceeds could help him cover a potentially multibillion-dollar tax obligation.

As per Forbes, Zuckerberg’s net worth is $239.3 billion. The CEO may immediately sell 20% of those new Class C shares, representing 10% of his total economic interest, to pay for his potential tax obligation while retaining voting control over Meta.

Meta’s special board committee said it was "critically important" for Zuckerberg to remain in leadership and operate from the company’s California headquarters amid "unprecedented challenge and competition" driven by AI.

Read Also: Mark Zuckerberg Says Muse Could Out-Earn Facebook, Instagram Per User, But Analyst Warns It’s 'Losing' More Money Than Any Other Product Meta Has Launched

California’s Billionaire Tax Sparks Debate

The agreement follows a broader debate over California’s proposed billionaire tax.

Earlier this month, Rep. Ro Khanna (D-Calif.) described the measure as an effort to update taxation as wealth becomes increasingly concentrated. Khanna compared the proposal with Wisconsin’s adoption of an income tax in 1911, arguing that tax systems must change alongside the ways wealth is created.

Last month, Sen. Bernie Sanders (I-Vt.) argued that the proposed 5% billionaire wealth tax in California could preserve health coverage for 3 million residents, accusing billionaires of spending $229 million to oppose the measure.

On the other hand, economist Peter Schiff had warned that the proposed billionaire tax could drive wealthy entrepreneurs, including Mark Zuckerberg, out of the state, forcing asset sales and potentially eroding its tax base.

Meta’s Stock Plan Signals More AI Spending

On Wednesday, Meta announced a non-voting stock recapitalization. Beginning Jan. 19, 2027, shareholders will receive one Class C share for each Class A and Class B share, to raise capital, compensate employees and finance acquisitions without diluting existing shareholders’ voting power.

The change was approved by entities linked to Mark Zuckerberg and his wife, Priscilla Chan, which control 56.1% of Meta’s voting power, eliminating the need for a shareholder vote. Meta expects to sell the shares periodically.

Nicholas Mugalli, CEO and principal of World Trade Securities, saw the plan as a sign of "more capex coming," with 2026 capex already guided at $135 billion to $145 billion.

Meta reported third-quarter revenue of $64.6 billion, topping analyst estimates of $63.37 billion, according to Benzinga Pro. Adjusted earnings came in at $7.40 per share, above expectations of $5.74.

Benzinga’s Edge Rankings place Meta in the 77th percentile for quality and the 75th percentile for growth, reflecting its strong performance in both areas. Benzinga’s screener allows you to compare META’s performance with its peers.

Price Action: On a year-to-date basis, Meta stock climbed 5.67%, as per Benzinga Pro. The stock traded 0.65% lower at $692.98 premarket on Thursday.

On Wednesday, Meta Platforms, Inc. (NASDAQ:META) CEO Mark Zuckerberg outlined the company’s long-term AI strategy, highlighting personal superintelligence, proprietary AI models and smart glasses as key bets that could shape its next phase of growth.

Zuckerberg Says Personal Superintelligence Is Meta’s North Star

During Meta’s third-quarter 2026 earnings call, Bernstein analyst Mark Shmulik asked Zuckerberg whether the company was entering a new era with its Muse AI models at the center of its business.

Zuckerberg said Meta’s vision of personal superintelligence builds on its longstanding mission to empower individuals and help people connect.

He pointed to a letter he wrote more than a year ago outlining personal superintelligence as the "North Star" guiding the company’s work, adding that Meta wants to put the power of advanced AI into everyone’s hands.

Read Also: Meta Strikes 8-Year Deal to Keep Mark Zuckerberg in California as Billionaire Tax Looms: ‘Critically Important’ for Him to Remain in Leadership

Meta Wants to Build Its Own AI Models and Agents

Zuckerberg said Meta has worked toward this vision for some time, including restructuring its AI efforts and establishing a dedicated lab to develop models for personal AI agents.

He argued that Meta can deliver the best user experience by developing and controlling the entire technology stack, from underlying AI models to the agents people interact with.

Smart Glasses Fit Into Meta’s Long-Term AI Strategy

The tech billionaire also connected Meta’s AI ambitions to its hardware investments, particularly smart glasses and other next-generation devices.

He said the company has long sought to develop new hardware platforms that can deliver better end-to-end experiences, adding that he expects these efforts to come together further in the coming years.

Zuckerberg Prioritizes Long-Term Technology Bets

Zuckerberg described AI and hardware investments as long-term bets, arguing that Meta’s priority should be building compelling technology for billions of people.

"As long as we continue to do that, then over time the business takes care of itself," he said.

Meta Beats Q3 Estimates, Raises 2026 Expense Outlook

Meta reported third-quarter revenue of $64.6 billion, surpassing analyst estimates of $63.37 billion. Adjusted earnings came in at $7.40 per share, topping expectations of $5.74 per share.

For the fourth quarter, Meta expects revenue of $73 billion to $76 billion, compared with analyst estimates of $73.74 billion.

The company raised its full-year 2026 expense forecast to $175 billion to $179 billion, up from its previous projection of $165 billion to $169 billion.

news.content:
The largest publicly listed Australian data center operator, NextDC, fell 44% on Wednesday after cutting its earnings guidance and deferring projects tied to its flagship M3 facility in Melbourne.

Power access was the cause, as residents pushed back on replacing wooden poles with 72ft-tall concrete pylons, delaying the facility’s power upgrade and highlighting the fragility of data center expansion.

The firm lowered its full-year earnings forecast by more than a third and lowered its revenue outlook.

“With M3 revenue deferred, we have paused projects not backed by customer contracts and put that capital behind the capacity behind our customers that have already contracted,” Chief Executive Officer Craig Scroggie said according to the Financial Times. The company reported 8.7 billion Australian dollars ($6.1 billion) of liquidity at the end of last month.

RBC Capital Markets analyst Tom Beadle called the delay an “incrementally negative development.” In a note, he wrote that community concerns “present a real risk to the timing of delivery of contracted capacity for data centre owners.” He still rates the stock as an outperform.

However, the tide has turned against the industry. Victoria’s Premier Ben Carroll has banned data centers near schools, childcare centers and homes; while Firmus, a data center firm backed by NVIDIA Corporation (NASDAQ:NVDA), canceled a $30 billion IPO earlier this month.

See More: Top Growth Stocks

The Case Against the Infrastructure

The selloff supports Jim Chanos’s argument. “You should own the companies that build the models, not the companies that build the data centers,” the short seller said, according to Business Insider. “The former are technology companies, the latter are REITs.”

AI chips last only a few years, so operators are stuck paying for repeated upgrades to power and cooling, according to an Asia Times analysis.

In the U.S. – two REITs face such risks, each in its own way. Digital Realty Trust Inc. (NYSE:DLR) focuses on scale, primarily serving wholesale hyperscale customers such as Amazon.com Inc. (NASDAQ:AMZN) and Microsoft Corp. (NASDAQ:MSFT). Because it operates massive facilities, it faces external bottlenecks when scaling to meet demand.

Meanwhile, Equinix Inc. (NASDAQ:EQIX) focuses on a dense ecosystem of interconnected customers, serving thousands of businesses rather than relying on a few large hyperscalers.

However, short seller Hindenburg Research previously accused the company of overselling its power capacity by as much as 175%, raising concerns about potential infrastructure strain.

For now, the U.S. picture is less severe than in Australia. According to Tom’s Hardware, SemiAnalysis found that more than 300 local moratoriums have held up only about 2.3 gigawatts of capacity, against 38 gigawatts expected to come online in 2027.

“We think moratoriums COULD delay the buildout, but they just aren’t yet at scale,” the firm said.

The bigger danger is to future projects in the pipeline. Texas Governor Greg Abbott told the Texas Commission on Environmental Quality to issue no permits for data center projects.

Law firm Bracewell expects that pause to last until the Electric Reliability Council finishes its review in mid-December, while New York has also imposed a pause through executive action.

Futurum Group CEO Daniel Newman said Wednesday he added to his position in CoreWeave Inc. (NASDAQ:CRWV), while stating that the selloff across artificial intelligence cloud providers was overdone.

The stock is down more than 5% in premarket trading on Thursday.

Calls the Selloff a ‘Psyop’

In a post on X, Newman said that the neocloud drawdown of the past 10 days was “basically a psyop,’”adding that results from Space Exploration Technologies Corp. and Meta Platforms Inc. “further validate the wildly asymmetric demand for compute and power.”

“I did get longer on CoreWeave,” Newman told Fox Business, pointing to a 246% year-over-year jump in its revenue backlog, not counting $25 billion in additional commitments this quarter.

“We are completely missing the point,” he added.

He said its capacity is sold out and that it is anchored by Microsoft Corp.‘s balance sheet, Meta and Jane Street, with more customers expanding beyond them.

Pointing to SpaceX’s results, Newman said companies with power and capacity can sell it “multiple times over” and “do well, even if we do have some bumps in the meantime.”

Read Also: Meta Has a New ‘North Star’ — Mark Zuckerberg Explains Why He’s Betting Big on Personal Superintelligence, AI Models and Smart Glasses

Why CRWV Fell

CoreWeave, a neocloud provider, has taken on more than $51 billion in debt and obligations to build out its AI infrastructure, and stock and bond investors are pushing back on how much it is spending.

Yields on CoreWeave debt continued to climb over the month, with the yield to maturity on its 9.75% bond due in 2031 reaching a high of 15.75% on Oct. 14, according to TradingView. Yields were at 14.85% at the time of writing.

SPCX Eased the Pressure

The stock went in the green for a while on Wednesday after Musk said on SpaceX’s earnings call that the company was being “hounded relentlessly by every hyperscaler” for compute and could rent it out “several times over.”

Of the 29 analysts covering the stock, 24 rate it Buy or Strong Buy, three Hold and two Sell, with a consensus price target of $133, according to Benzinga Pro.

Price Action: Shares closed 0.50% lower on Wednesday at $61.82 and fell 5.45% to $58.45 in premarket trading on Thursday.

Over the past month, the stock is down 27.64% and 13.67% so far this year. Over the past year, the stock is down 50.57%.

news.content:
Nvidia Corp. (NASDAQ:NVDA) CEO Jensen Huang stated that token consumption and graphics processing unit demand have gone “through the roof” due to artificial intelligence agents. Deepwater Asset Management Managing Partner Gene Munster supported this statement, predicting that daily bot users could reach the billions in the coming years and drive compute demand.

Gene Munster Backs Bullish Outlook

Munster echoed Huang’s comments, stating that the rise of personalized agents is “one of the clearer reasons compute demand should keep ramping for the next few years”. Munster estimated that agents can consume “10-15x the tokens of a chatbot.”

Currently, about 15 million consumers use bots daily, Munster noted. However, he predicted that “in a few years that could be billions,” which would fuel sustained growth for Nvidia.

Chief Market Strategist Shay Boloor similarly noted that agents already consume approximately five times more tokens than human users on the OpenRouter platform, stating that “AI compute demand will keep growing for years”.

Read Also: Nokia Teams Up with Super Micro on Nvidia-Based AI-RAN. Here’s the Setup for Nokia Stock

Agents Drive Token Usage

During his keynote address in Berlin on Oct. 21, Huang discussed the emergence of personalized AI agents, specifically highlighting “the incredible Meta Muse, Grok bot, and of course Gemini.” Huang explained that agents “think, reason, iterate, use tools, and as a result consume an enormous amount of tokens.”

Because agents iterate to solve complex problems, they become more capable and are adopted by a wider user base. As agents must “use a lot of tokens to think, the amount of token consumption has gone through the roof,” Huang said. He added that “GPU demand has really gone through the roof” as a direct result.

The Architecture of AI Agents

Huang outlined five elements of an AI agent: a model, an exoskeleton that orchestrates memory and tools, a sandbox that provides isolation, knowledge and tools. He characterized the harness as an “exoskeleton” that orchestrates work and allows the agent to engage working memory and long-term memory.

This architecture requires dedicated computing power for processing the large language model, managing the agent’s knowledge data, and executing the tools it needs to perform tasks autonomously. He noted that the industry is shifting from simply consuming AI to manufacturing it within massive data centers, which he referred to as AI factories.

How Has NVDA Performed in 2026?

The stock was 2.41% lower in premarket trading on Thursday. It advanced by 22.53% over the last year, up 19.02% year-to-date, and down 2.38% over the last month. The stock closed up 2.54% at $221.97 on Wednesday.

news.content:
Nokia Corp. (NYSE:NOK) reported stronger-than-expected third-quarter earnings Thursday as growing demand from artificial intelligence and cloud customers boosted data-center networking sales, offsetting sluggish spending by traditional telecom operators.

The Finnish telecommunications equipment maker also benefited from converting part of its data-center equipment backlog into revenue.

However, Nokia shares fell in premarket trading as investors weighed weaker reported operating profit, higher restructuring costs and a reduced free cash flow conversion outlook.

Nokia Earnings Beat Wall Street Estimates

Nokia reported third-quarter net sales of 5.15 billion euros ($5.93 billion), up 10% year over year and 9% on a constant-currency basis. Revenue exceeded analysts’ estimate of $5.80 billion.

Adjusted earnings of 10 cents per share beat the consensus estimate of 8 cents.

Network Infrastructure revenue rose 15% year over year, driven by 43% growth in IP Networks and 18% growth in Optical Networks.

Mobile Infrastructure revenue increased 5%, supported by Radio Networks and Technology Standards.

See More: Top Quality Stocks

AI Data Center Demand Fuels Growth

AI and Cloud revenue surged 126% year over year, accounting for 12.2% of total sales. Nokia also secured 1.5 billion euros in orders from AI and cloud customers during the quarter.

CEO Justin Hotard is expanding Nokia’s presence in data-center networking as weak 5G investment weighs on traditional telecom spending.

The company’s acquisition of Infinera supports that strategy. Nokia expects to complete the integration by the end of 2026 and generate about 200 million euros in cost savings.

Nokia also expects its broader Optical and IP Networks businesses to grow 25% to 30% in 2027.

Meanwhile, Nokia is working with NVIDIA Corp. (NASDAQ:NVDA) to develop mobile-network equipment using advanced chips, extending its AI strategy into communications networks.

Supply Shortages Threaten Expansion

Rapid AI infrastructure investment has tightened supplies of memory chips and other components, increasing costs across the industry.

Hotard told Bloomberg Thursday that customers are increasingly aware of potential shortages and are adjusting their purchasing decisions.

Mobile Infrastructure sales rose 5% to 2.9 billion euros, exceeding analysts’ estimate of 2.8 billion euros. The increase partly reflected revenue pulled forward from the fourth quarter.

Nokia is expanding optical-networking capacity, including a second facility in San Jose expected to become fully operational by the end of October. However, semiconductor supply constraints remain a challenge.

Restructuring Costs Weigh on Profit

Nokia raised its full-year restructuring cost forecast to as much as 1.1 billion euros from 800 million euros.

Reported operating profit fell 22% to 196 million euros, while the operating margin narrowed to 3.8% from 5.4%.

However, comparable operating profit rose 35% to 605 million euros. The comparable operating margin improved 220 basis points to 11.7%.

The contrasting results highlight Nokia’s challenge of balancing stronger AI-related demand with restructuring expenses, supply constraints and subdued telecom investment.

Nokia Maintains Full-Year Profit Outlook

Nokia reaffirmed its 2026 comparable operating profit forecast of 2.1 billion euros to 2.6 billion euros.

The company expects Network Infrastructure sales to grow 12% to 14% on a constant-currency and portfolio basis. It also raised its growth assumption for Optical and IP Networks to slightly above its previous 18% to 20% forecast.

For the fourth quarter, Nokia expects revenue to increase 20% to 24% sequentially, implying sales of approximately $7.12 billion to $7.36 billion. Analysts expect revenue of $7.30 billion.

Nokia expects a strong sequential increase in fourth-quarter comparable operating profit, lifting its full-year result above the midpoint of its guidance range.

However, the company lowered its full-year free cash flow conversion forecast to 35% to 55%, citing higher working capital investment and accelerated restructuring costs.

news.content:
Bitcoin (CRYPTO: BTC) sold off sharply during Asian trading hours after failing to hold a breakout above $84,300, leaving bulls who bought the move trapped as prices reversed lower.

Why Bitcoin’s Breakout Attempt Failed

Widely-followed cryptocurrency trader JDK Analysis posted on X that Bitcoin pushed strongly above its monthly value-weighted average price and local value area high during New York trading, backed by spot buying and fresh long positions. 

That momentum stalled near $84,300 as passive sellers absorbed large market buy orders and prevented the price from moving higher.

When Asian trading began, price retreated back toward that same breakout zone, and buyers failed to defend it. 

JDK compared the setup to a football team pushing too many players forward, losing possession and leaving itself exposed to a counterattack.

If the breakout fails, those committed buyers are now trapped, and their exits fuel the move down,” JDK wrote. 

“That’s exactly what we saw: longs and spot buyers committed to the attack, then found themselves trapped as it stalled,” he added.

Four Reasons Asian Markets Bled $600 Billion

Widely-followed market commentator Bull Theory posted on X that Asian stock markets lost more than $600 billion in value during the same stretch, pointing to four factors behind the move:

  • US futures weakness: S&P 500 (NYSE:SPY) futures fell 0.8% and Nasdaq futures dropped 1.6%, dragging Asian markets lower.
  • Iran tensions: President Donald Trump said the U.S. is “not negotiating” with Iran, adding fresh geopolitical uncertainty.
  • AI stock concerns: semiconductor and AI-linked stocks fell across Asia as investors question returns on massive AI spending.
  • Oil prices: crude climbing above $100 per barrel revived inflation fears and concerns that central banks keep rates higher for longer.

Why ETF Flows Stayed Positive Despite the Selloff

Even as Bitcoin’s price reversed, demand through regulated channels held up. SoSoValue data showed U.S. spot Bitcoin ETFs took in $528.40 million on October 21, led by BlackRock’s (NYSE:BLK) IBIT (NASDAQ:IBIT) at $234.99 million and Fidelity’s FBTC (BATS:FBTC) at $212.71 million.

The divergence between falling spot prices and rising ETF inflows suggests institutional buyers kept accumulating while the Asian session selloff flushed leveraged traders out of the market.

news.content:
Meta Platforms Inc. (NASDAQ:META) remains at the center of the artificial intelligence investment debate as analysts weigh strong advertising growth and the long-term potential of its Muse AI platform against soaring capital spending and uncertainty over monetization.

Meta reported third-quarter revenue of $64.6 billion, up 26% year over year and above analysts’ estimate of $63.37 billion. Adjusted earnings of $7.40 per share beat the $5.74 consensus estimate.

Ad impressions increased 10%, while the average price per ad rose 14%. However, free cash flow turned negative at $2.12 billion.

For the fourth quarter, Meta forecast revenue of $73 billion to $76 billion, compared with the $73.74 billion consensus estimate.

The company also raised its 2026 capital expenditure outlook to $135 billion to $145 billion and increased its expense guidance to $175 billion to $179 billion.

Wagner Says Capex Concerns Look Overblown

Aptus Capital Advisors portfolio manager David Wagner told CNBC on Thursday that concerns around Meta’s rising debt and AI spending are overstated because hyperscalers still carry much stronger debt coverage than the broader market.

He said that Meta may raise more debt or equity as spending climbs, but he sees no sign that AI investment is slowing. Wagner argued that one company’s capital spending becomes another company’s revenue, supporting the broader AI ecosystem.

He remains bullish on Meta and believes the burden of proof still sits with AI bears.

Munster Calls Muse Meta’s Future

Deepwater Asset Management Managing Partner Gene Munster told CNBC on Thursday that Muse represents Meta’s future platform and could eventually reshape engagement across Facebook, Instagram and WhatsApp.

He sees commerce as the leading near-term use case and believes personalized agents could eventually handle product discovery and transactions across the internet.

Munster estimated Muse may currently have roughly 10 million daily users, leaving substantial room for growth against Meta’s multibillion-user ecosystem.

He also expects Meta’s AI spending to rise further. With Street expectations near $196 billion in 2027 capex, Munster said spending could ultimately exceed $225 billion. He also expects Meta may need to raise another $25 billion-$50 billion in capital.

See More: Top Momentum Stocks

Wang Says Advertising Remains Strong

Constellation Research’s Ray Wang told CNBC on Thursday that Meta is using its large data sets to create a consumer AI flywheel between Muse, advertising and its social platforms.

He believes Muse can strengthen engagement while driving additional advertiser interest.

Wang also highlighted Meta’s advertising business, saying it remains strong, with election-year spending providing another potential tailwind.

Thill Wants More Detail on Muse

Jefferies senior software analyst Brent Thill told CNBC on Thursday that Meta delivered strong revenue growth and broadly steady fourth-quarter guidance, but investors need more visibility into Muse’s impact and the company’s 2027 spending trajectory.

He sees several potential Muse monetization paths, including advertising, subscriptions, token purchases and AI-enabled devices.

Thill also expects AI capital expenditures across hyperscalers to rise materially in 2027, potentially pressuring free cash flow in the near term.

Across the four views, Meta’s core ad business and Muse adoption support the bull case, while capital intensity, financing needs and the timing of AI monetization remain the key challenges.

Information technology rose 1.67%, industrials added 0.91%, and financials gained 0.57%, while communication services fell 1.11%, real estate slipped 0.76%, and consumer staples declined 0.73%.

Insights From Analysts

Jeremy Siegel, senior economist to WisdomTree and emeritus professor of finance at The Wharton School of the University of Pennsylvania, wrote that the AI buildout has become a key force shaping technology stocks, long-term interest rates, and rotation between growth and value.

He said, “The biggest driver of long-term rates right now is not oil and may not even be what the Federal Reserve does at its next meeting. It is the enormous demand for capital associated with the AI buildout.”

Siegel also said that if AI spending or token demand disappoints, he could see “a 20% to 30% correction in Nasdaq,” while the S&P 500 could decline “only 5% to 10%.”

He added, “I still do not expect the Fed to raise rates in October,” while calling December less certain and saying he would put the probability of a hike “extremely high.”

Upcoming Economic Data

Here’s what investors will be keeping an eye on Thursday.

  • Initial Jobless Claims: For the week ending October 17, seasonally adjusted initial unemployment claims fell by 6,000 to a total of 194,000. The four-week moving average for initial claims also saw a slight decline, edging down to 197,750.

news.content:
Nvidia Corp. (NASDAQ:NVDA) CEO Jensen Huang said the company’s AI computing systems could retain enough value to support financing, potentially changing how lenders evaluate infrastructure investments.

During an interview with Deirdre Bosa of Yahoo Finance on Wednesday, on the sidelines of Nvidia’s GTC Berlin conference, Huang discussed AI compute becoming more tradable.

He said Nvidia’s systems are ‘productive,’ ‘fungible’ and ‘durable’. Their useful lives could extend eight years or longer, he said, compared with the four-year replacement cycle commonly assumed by investors and lenders.

As GPU futures markets and flexible spot pricing develop, Nvidia’s hardware could build significant residual value. Huang said lenders may eventually use that equipment as collateral when underwriting debt.

“The risk involved in underwriting Nvidia’s assets, in our Nvidia computing, is the lowest of any asset out there, and so I think this is an area that’s going to really play into our advantage,” the CEO said.

Huang said financing will be essential to expanding AI infrastructure. Nvidia’s computing assets could lower lending risk because the systems remain useful across multiple customers, workloads and applications.

He added that Nvidia’s compute already carries “really, really high” residual value, although financial markets have not fully recognized or reflected that value in financing decisions. “Nobody gives a credit for that,” Huang added.

Read Also: Amazon Just Found a Way Around Nvidia’s Biggest Moat

Nvidia’s AI Boom Raises Debt Risks

Nvidia’s AI boom is increasingly tied to private credit, with CoreWeave Inc (NASDAQ: CRWV) and other AI cloud providers borrowing billions against Nvidia GPUs and data center assets to fund infrastructure expansion.

In August, Nvidia announced partnerships with Apollo Global Management Inc. (NYSE: APO), BlackRock Inc. (NYSE: BLK), Blackstone Inc. (NYSE: BX), Brookfield Asset Management (NYSE: BAM), Goldman Sachs and KKR & Co. Inc. (NYSE: KKR) to mobilize more than $500 billion in third-party capital over time to finance AI infrastructure development. The company is positioning its GPUs as investable assets, citing their long lifespan, low token costs, revenue potential, and broad ecosystem of customers using its CUDA platform.

However, investor Michael Burry criticized Nvidia’s plan to mobilize over $500 billion for AI infrastructure, calling it a "Wall Street stunt" involving opaque private-credit arrangements. He questioned Nvidia taking 25% stakes and providing residual-value guarantees on chip purchases, arguing that routing the financing through private equity and private credit could reproduce existing risks under a new structure.

Price Action: Year-to-date, Nvidia stock surged 19.02%, as per Benzinga Pro. During Thursday’s pre-market trading session, it was trading 2.45% lower at $216.53.

news.author: Erica Kollmann
news.content:
Meta Platforms Inc. (NASDAQ:META) plans to create a new class of non-voting shares it can use to raise capital, pay employees and buy other companies as it pours money into AI. A close read of the company’s filing, however, turns up two drawbacks.

  • META stock is moving after earnings. Get all the details here. 

The Facebook parent company announced the plan with its third-quarter results, declaring a one-time dividend of one Class C share for every outstanding Class A and Class B share. The new class will take effect on Jan. 19, 2027. 

In its SEC filing, Meta said the Class C stock "will be available for use for capital raising, employee compensation, potential acquisitions, and other general corporate purposes."

The structure also protects CEO Mark Zuckerberg’s grip on the company, and Meta says so directly in the filing: "The Recapitalization will also allow us to make stock-based acquisitions and to continue to grant equity awards to our employees without affecting Mr. Zuckerberg’s majority voting control.”

Zuckerberg controls about 60.6% of the vote at Meta while owning roughly 13.4% of the company. Fortune reported that he wanted to keep his control, meet his pledges to fund the Chan Zuckerberg Initiative with Meta stock and prepare for a possible California wealth tax. 

Zuckerberg can sell 20% of his new Class C shares right away.  

Read Also: Anthropic Has Over $600 Billion in Compute Contracts — And It's Not Enough

A Cheaper Currency

The first drawback is price. According to the filing, Meta expects Class C shares to trade at a discount to its voting stock. 

A lower share price would force the company to issue more stock to raise the same amount or pay for the same deal, and existing shareholders would absorb more dilution.

Zuckerberg raised the issue himself during talks with the special committee, warning the dividend ratio could leave Class C shares at a significant discount to Class A stock in a later equity raise and hurt all shareholders. 

See More: Top Growth Stocks

A Tax Problem for Sellers

The second drawback applies to acquisitions. According to the filing, Class C shares cannot meet the voting-stock requirements for certain tax-deferred deals.

Owners of a target company hoping to defer a tax bill may hold out for a different form of payment, which would limit the new shares’ usefulness in dealmaking.

The Bottom Line

Meta’s need for capital is easy to understand, given third-quarter capex of $34.91 billion left free cash flow at negative $2.12 billion. The company expects 2026 capex of $135 billion to $145 billion and plans to keep investing aggressively in AI next year. 

The market will get its first chance to price the Class C shares once they arrive in January.
